h: Brains, bikes and the best of the city
p: Cambridge folk love a puzzle, so don't be surprised if the competitive streak comes out in your group. To give yourselves a fighting chance, nominate someone to keep track of time and someone to keep found objects together. Search properly before you start solving: many teams waste minutes trying to crack a code when the missing piece is sitting in a drawer they haven't opened yet. And if you're stuck, swap jobs around. Fresh eyes work wonders.

It's a lovely thing to do with visiting friends or family who've already seen the big sights, and a decent way to break up a long day of walking. University students will find it a fun way to celebrate the end of exams, too. It's a good one for a first date with a difference, as well, because there's never an awkward silence when there's a padlock to open.

St Andrew's Street is right on the doorstep of some cracking places. Emmanuel College sits on the same street, and the city's famous college buildings stretch away towards the river from here. King's College Chapel is a must for its soaring fan-vaulted ceiling, while the Fitzwilliam Museum on Trumpington Street is free to visit and stuffed with treasures from around the world. Kettle's Yard is a quieter gem for art lovers, and the University Botanic Garden near the station is a peaceful spot for a stroll. For something different, Mill Road is the city's independent, multicultural high street, full of cafes and food from around the world. Drummer Street bus station is very close by, which makes getting in and out on public transport straightforward.
